'''Janet Louise Smith''' is the Margaret J. Hunter Collegiate Professor in the [[Life Sciences Institute]], director of the Center for [[Structural biology|Structural Biology]] at the [[University of Michigan, Ann Arbor|University of Michigan]], professor of [[Biochemistry|biological chemistry]] and [[biophysics]] at the [[University of Michigan, Ann Arbor|University of Michigan]], and research professor in the [[Life Sciences Institute]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://mmheadlines.org/2016/09/janet-smith-lauded-with-lectureship-award/|title=JANET SMITH LAUDED WITH LECTURESHIP AWARD|website=Michigan Medicine Headlines|access-date=August 9, 2019|date=September 15, 2016}}</ref> Additionally, she is the scientific director of The General Medical Sciences and Cancer Institutes’ structural biology facility at the [[Advanced Photon Source]] (GM/CA @ APS).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gmca.aps.anl.gov/staff/|title=GM/CA Staff|website=gmca.aps.anl.gov|access-date=2019-08-10}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |title=New Beamlines Dedicated At Argonne |url=http://pubsapp.acs.org/cen/news/83/i27/8327notw7.html? |last=MITCH JACOBY |journal=Chemical & Engineering News | issn=0009-2347 |date=2005-06-29}}</ref>

== Biography ==

Smith is native of [[Pennsylvania]] and studied chemistry as a National Merit Scholar at [[Indiana University of Pennsylvania]] (BS, 1973).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.purdue.edu/research/awards/herbert-newby-mccoy-award/past/smith.php|title=2001 McCoy Award Recipient|website=purdue.edu|access-date=2019-08-10|archive-date=2019-08-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190810012817/https://www.purdue.edu/research/awards/herbert-newby-mccoy-award/past/smith.php|url-status=dead}}</ref> She continued her study at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison|University of Wisconsin-Madison]] (Ph.D., 1978) in structure in biology under Dr. M. Sundaralingam supervision.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pharmacy.wisc.edu/event/2019-hutchinson-lecture-janet-smith-phd/|title=2019 Hutchinson Lecture – Dr. Janet Smith|website=School of Pharmacy|access-date=2019-08-10|archive-date=2019-08-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190810013250/https://pharmacy.wisc.edu/event/2019-hutchinson-lecture-janet-smith-phd/|url-status=dead}}</ref> she continued to do her postdoctoral work with [[Wayne Hendrickson]] at the [[United States Naval Research Laboratory|Naval Research Laboratory]] as a National Research Council Research Fellow.

== Research ==

Smith's research group focus on the understanding of proteins to the molecular level through structural biology. The main experimental technique employed in her lab is [[X-ray crystallography]] used to elucidate protein structures. Some of her research findings solved [[Crystal structure]]s. Janet's lab has also worked towards method development for rapid structure determination.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lsi.umich.edu/science/our-labs/janet-smith-lab|title=Janet Smith Lab|date=2018-02-23|website=Life Sciences Institute|access-date=2019-08-10}}</ref> Her lab contributed to the development of [[multiwavelength anomalous diffraction]] (MAD) used routinely for structure determination.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lsi.umich.edu/science/our-labs/smith-lab/research|title=Smith Lab – Research|date=2018-02-23|website=Life Sciences Institute|access-date=2019-08-10}}</ref>

Her research group have revealed the molecular structure of a protein produced by the [[Zika virus]] that is thought to be involved in the virus's reproduction and its interaction with a host's [[immune system]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2016/07/160725121717.htm|title=Researchers 'solve' key Zika virus protein structure|last=|first=|date=July 25, 2016|website=ScienceDaily|language=en|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-03-23}}</ref>
